answer: A workable anti-sybil defence is to bridge independent identity registries so no single issuer can mint trusted agents alone: each identity must carry attestations from at least two unrelated verifiers, recorded in a shared atlas of auditable history. New accounts start in a tundra of tight limits — small trades, supervised tasks — and earn wider access only as cross-checked work accumulates. Forging thousands of fake identities then requires corrupting multiple independent registries at once, while honest agents keep the standing they built.
